title: Complementary p-basis monomial spanning
statement:
Let p be prime and k a field of characteristic p [def-weil-field]. Let I be any index type and t : I → k. Assume that the bounded finitely supported monomials in t form a basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module] of k over F_p(k^p), precisely as expressed by hpb below. Let J be a finite subset of I and kJ the subfield generated by all pth powers and all t_i with i outside J, precisely as expressed by hkJ below. Then the bounded J-monomials span k over kJ. Complete formal statement: theorem pBasisComplementMonomialBasis_spanning
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharP k p]
    (I : Type w) (t : I → k)
    (hpb : ∃ b : Module.Basis
      {E : I →₀ ℕ // ∀ i : I, E i < p}
      (IntermediateField.adjoin (ZMod p) (Set.range (fun x : k ↦ x ^ p))) k,
      ∀ E, b E = (E : I →₀ ℕ).prod (fun i e ↦ t i ^ e))
    (J : Finset I) (kJ : Subfield k)
    (hkJ : kJ = Subfield.closure
      (Set.range (fun x : k ↦ x ^ p) ∪ {x : k | ∃ i : I, i ∉ J ∧ t i = x})) :
    ⊤ ≤ Submodule.span kJ (Set.range (fun E : J → Fin p ↦ ∏ i : J, t i ^ (E i : ℕ)))

proof.text:
Put F = F_p(k^p). By the closure universal property, F is contained in kJ:
prime-field elements are natural-number casts and pth powers are generators of kJ.
For a bounded finitely supported exponent E, use Finsupp.filter to partition E
between J and its complement. The complementary product belongs to kJ by closure
under powers and finite products. The J part equals the displayed monomial indexed
by i ↦ E(i) in Fin p, using the exponent bounds and extending its support to J with
zero exponents. Their product belongs to the kJ-span by scalar multiplication.
Expand any x using the given F-basis and its finitely supported coordinate vector.
Each summand belongs to the kJ-span because its F-coordinate belongs to kJ; closure
under finite sums finishes the proof. No grouping of repeated J restrictions is
needed. This also handles empty J, empty I, and zero exponents.
